items.title: What does the series do?
items.text:
• The BCP-007 series of AMWA Best Common Practices define how to connect Endpoints using AMWA IS-04 and IS-05 for various transports including:
  • Specification of the resources and attributes used for the format.
  • Requirements for the Transport File (such as SDP).
  • Examples.
path: [Work In Progress] AMWA NMOS Transport Mappings

items.title: Why does it matter?
items.text:
• The individual mapping BCPs ensure consistency between implementations offering NMOS for each stream transport.
  • Bringing these together in the BCP-007 series helps provide consistency between the individual mappings and provides an index of mappings.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
Choose the mapping for the transport being integrated:

  • BCP-007-01 for NDI
  • BCP-007-02 for IPMX/USB
  • BCP-007-03 for MXL

There is more information about the NMOS Specifications and their GitHub repos at https://specs.amwa.tv/nmos.

items.title: AMWA BCP-007 NMOS Transport Mappings: Overview
Introduction
items.text:
AMWA IS-04/05 and the other NMOS Specifications were originally mostly used in ST 2110 RTP environments, but have always been capable of extension to other streaming transports. BCP-007 is an extensible series of mappings specifying how to use NMOS for individual transports.

BCP-007 is complemented by the BCP-006 series of format mappings.

For details of the current set of mappings see the list of BCPs on the main NMOS page.

items.title: Style Guide
items.text:
Be careful with normative and non-normative language.

It may be better to put lengthy guidance in a separate implementation guide.

Markdown will be linted, so try to keep consistent with what is in this template and what is in other specs. See https://github.com/AMWA-TV/nmos-lint-scripts for details.
